svg.text: B3 — Breast lesions of uncertain malignant potential
FRCS Part 1 (General Surgery) · the B1–B5 core-biopsy code · ADH · FEA · papilloma · radial scar · the VAE pathway
THE CORE-BIOPSY B CODE · WHERE B3 SITS
B3 is a reporting CODE, not a diagnosis — it flags a lesion needing further tissue before cancer can be excluded. The four ductal/epithelial B3 lesions are shown below.
THE FOUR DUCTAL / EPITHELIAL B3 LESIONS
Low if small / no atypia; ~14% with
THE ONE RULE THAT TRIAGES B3 · ATYPIA PRESENT vs ABSENT
~29% upgrade to in-situ or invasive cancer.
The more atypia, the lower the threshold for surgical excision over VAE.
Benign B3 fully sampled — avoids open surgery.
In-situ or invasive cancer on excision.
Definitive breast + axillary management via MDT.
Papilloma WITH atypia and cellular fibroepithelial / ?phyllodes lesions need diagnostic surgical excision — architecture cannot be
B3 is a biopsy CODE, not a diagnosis — it means ‘needs more tissue’, not benign and not cancer.
ADH vs low-grade DCIS is only a matter of extent — <2 mm or ≤2 duct spaces is ADH; always report the size.
A radial scar is spiculated on mammography and mimics carcinoma — the diagnosis is histological, never radiological
Atypia anywhere in a B3 roughly doubles the upgrade risk (~29% vs ~13%) — lower your threshold for excision.
Papilloma with atypia and cellular fibroepithelial lesions are the B3s that still need open surgical excision, not VAE.
Classical LCIS / ALH is B3, but pleomorphic LCIS behaves like DCIS and is managed as B5 — do not lump them together.
Sources: RCPath / NHSBSP breast core-biopsy B-categories (B1–B5). NHS Breast Screening multidisciplinary working group guidelines for the diagnosis and management of B3 lesions on
core biopsy (Pinder et al., Clinical Radiology 2018). Sloane Project — impact of vacuum-assisted excision on B3 lesions in the NHSBSP, England.
Key numbers: overall B3 upgrade ~16.6%; with atypia ~29% vs ~13% without (Sloane). Since the 2018 guideline, most B3 lesions have second-line vacuum-assisted excision rather than
